page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor architecture. Operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz, this server features 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core allocation. The hardware configuration includes 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps. No GPUs are present on this instance.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core capabilities. The server achieves top 10% performance in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU physics tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only and write large-block benchmarks placing in the top 10% tier. In database and caching workloads, the instance demonstrates top-tier throughput, specifically in Redis SET operations and Passmark database operations. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average middle 50% category.

The bare-metal design offers high resource density and direct hardware access, which translates to high qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage the 96 dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading overhead. The inclusion of 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD storage eliminates the need for external storage attachments for high-I/O tasks. This server is suited for multi-threaded CPU-bound workloads, software compilation, database hosting, high-throughput web serving, and medium-scale LLM text generation.
